details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu/vce1: Fix VCE 1 firmware size and offsets

The VCPU BO contains the actual FW at an offset, but
it was not calculated into the VCPU BO size.
Subtract this from the FW size to make sure there is
no out of bounds access.

Make sure the stack and data offsets are aligned to
the 32K TLB size.

Check that the FW microcode actually fits in the
space that is reserved for it.

(cherry picked from commit c16fe59f622a080fc457a57b3e8f14c780699449)

scenarios.value:
AV:L - An attacker reaches VCE1 through DRM command-submission ioctls on the local render device; there is no network or physical attack path.
AC:L - An attacker can repeatedly submit VCE jobs and control session allocation and engine power-up without winning an uncontrollable race or relying on an unusual runtime condition.
PR:L - The AMDGPU_CS ioctl is DRM_RENDER_ALLOW and contains no capability or DRM-master requirement, so ordinary users with render-node access can reach it.
UI:N - Exploitation requires only attacker-controlled ioctl submissions and does not depend on another user opening content or performing an action.
S:C - The VCE VCPU operates through direct GPU/GART addresses with its VM control disabled, so access beyond the kernel VCPU BO crosses the GPU DMA memory-isolation boundary.
C:H - The oversized and misaligned read/write cache windows can expose adjacent VRAM or GART-backed memory outside the VCPU BO, potentially permitting disclosure of high-value memory.
I:H - The VCE data and stack windows are writable, so their out-of-bounds placement can corrupt adjacent GPU or GART-backed allocations and potentially affect execution or protected data.
A:H - The invalid firmware layout can cause VCE VM faults, firmware failure, or a GPU/card lockup, and an unprivileged attacker can repeatedly reactivate the engine to reproduce the disruption.

descriptions.description: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

descriptions.value: vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.30.0, flash late-interaction scoring at the /score and /rerank endpoints derives each worker's query_key value from the caller-controlled X-Request-Id header. A concurrent request that reuses a victim's identifier can overwrite the cached query embedding so the victim's documents are scored against the attacker's query, and shared use counters can also cause a late-interaction cache-miss error. This issue is fixed in version 0.30.0.

Oracle heeft kwetsbaarheden verholpen in Oracle Financial Services Enterprise Case Management, Oracle Financial Services Regulatory Reporting en Oracle Financial Services Customer Screening, allen versie 8.1.2.10.
notes.title: Feiten

notes.text: De kwetsbaarheden betreffen meerdere Oracle Financial Services producten en maken het mogelijk voor aanvallers met verschillende niveaus van privileges en netwerktoegang via HTTP om ongeautoriseerd toegang te verkrijgen tot kritieke of gevoelige data. In Oracle Financial Services Enterprise Case Management kunnen laaggeprivilegieerde aanvallers data creëren, verwijderen of wijzigen, wat kan leiden tot verhoogde toegangsrechten of ongeautoriseerde toegang tot gevoelige informatie. Sommige kwetsbaarheden vereisen dat de aanvaller infrastructuurtoegang en hoge privileges heeft om vertrouwelijke data te benaderen. Andere kwetsbaarheden maken het mogelijk om zonder verhoogde privileges via netwerktoegang data te lezen en te schrijven. In Oracle Financial Services Regulatory Reporting kunnen laaggeprivilegieerde gebruikers met infrastructuurtoegang privileges escaleren en toegang krijgen tot kritieke data. In Oracle Financial Services Customer Screening kunnen niet-geauthenticeerde aanvallers via HTTP toegang krijgen tot gevoelige data zonder authenticatie.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/rds: use wq_has_sleeper() in release_in_xmit()

release_in_xmit() clears RDS_IN_XMIT with clear_bit_unlock() and then
checks waitqueue_active() to decide whether anyone needs waking.
clear_bit_unlock() is only a release operation: it orders the
critical section before the bit clear, but does not order the
subsequent plain load of the wait queue head after it.  The waiter
side does the mirror image - it adds itself to the wait queue and
then tests the bit.  That is the classic store-buffering pattern: the
releasing CPU can read the wait queue as empty while the waiting CPU
still reads the bit as set, so the sleeper is never woken.

The waiters are rds_conn_shutdown() and rds_tcp_reset_callbacks(),
both in uninterruptible wait_event() with no timeout.  A lost wake-up
strands the shutdown worker on its single-threaded workqueue until
some other sender releases the bit again - and on a connection that
is being torn down precisely because it failed, there may never be
another sender.

The barrier used to be there: release_in_xmit() did clear_bit()
followed by smp_mb__after_atomic() until commit 1422f28826d2 ("rds:
introduce acquire/release ordering in acquire/release_in_xmit()")
folded both into clear_bit_unlock(), which strengthened the lock
hand-off but silently dropped the full barrier the wake-up check
depends on.  The refill counterpart, release_refill() in
net/rds/ib_recv.c, still carries its smp_mb__after_atomic() for
exactly this reason.

Use wq_has_sleeper(), which is waitqueue_active() preceded by the
required full barrier.

Oracle heeft kwetsbaarheden verholpen in onder andere Oracle Communications Unified Assurance, Oracle Communications Billing and Revenue Management, Oracle Primavera Unifier, en Oracle Java SE. Daarnaast zijn fixes uitgebracht voor Ruby-componenten in Oracle Communication producten zoals Net::IMAP, Mail, Nokogiri, rubyzip en MessagePack, Node.js, OpenSSL, Curl, Libgcrypt, Libexpat, Puma, Containerd, Faraday, go-git, PCRE2, Apache Tomcat, Apache HTTP Server, Perl DBI, nghttp2, en andere open source libraries en tools.
notes.title: Feiten

notes.text: De kwetsbaarheden omvatten diverse typen beveiligingsproblemen zoals incorrecte cryptografische berekeningen, onvoldoende toegangsbeperkingen, heap buffer overflows, use-after-free fouten, denial-of-service door crashes of resource leaks, command injection, path traversal, memory corruptie, integer overflows, en onjuiste validatie van input. Aanvallers kunnen deze kwetsbaarheden misbruiken om onder meer ongeautoriseerde toegang te verkrijgen, gevoelige informatie te lekken, data te wijzigen, systemen te laten crashen, denial-of-service te veroorzaken, of in sommige gevallen volledige systeemcompromittering te bereiken. Sommige kwetsbaarheden vereisen authentificatie, andere kunnen door onbevoegde netwerkaanvallers worden geëxploiteerd. Er zijn ook kwetsbaarheden die specifiek impact hebben op bepaalde configuraties of functies, zoals persistent connections in Puma of OAuth token refresh in RabbitMQ.

cna.title: Gimp: out-of-bounds access, invalid free and use-after-free when processing xmc file comments

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the file-xmc plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted XMC image file, the plugin does not properly validate the comment subtype before using it as an array index. This missing validation leads to out-of-bounds memory access, invalid free and use-after-free issues. This vulnerability can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

cna.x_redhatCweChain: CWE-129: Improper Validation of Array Index

workarounds.value: To mitigate this vulnerability, do not open or import XMC files from untrusted sources with GIMP.

cna.title: Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 Reachable Assertion via ParsePFDEntry Orientation Tag

descriptions.value: Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.7 contain a reachable assertion vulnerability in ParsePFDEntry() that allows attackers to abort applications via an invalid orientation tag. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG XR file with an out-of-range WMP_tagTransformation value to crash applications using default assertion-enabled builds, or store an unchecked orientation value otherwise.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: Fix null-ptr-deref in fib6_nh_mtu_change().

fib6_nh_mtu_change() re-fetches idev via __in6_dev_get(arg->dev) and
dereferences idev->cnf.mtu6 without a NULL check. addrconf_ifdown()
clears dev->ip6_ptr with RCU_INIT_POINTER() after rt6_disable_ip() has
released tb6_lock, so the RA-driven MTU walk can observe a NULL idev and
oops. The caller rt6_mtu_change_route() guards its own __in6_dev_get(),
but this re-fetch is unguarded; nexthop-backed routes survive
addrconf_ifdown()'s flush, so the walk still reaches it after ip6_ptr is
nulled.

Return 0 when idev is NULL, matching rt6_mtu_change_route() and the
fib6_mtu() fix in commit 5ad509c1fdad ("ipv6: Fix null-ptr-deref in
fib6_mtu().").

  Oops: general protection fault, ... KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range
        [0x00000000000002a8-0x00000000000002af]
  RIP: 0010:fib6_nh_mtu_change+0x203/0x990
   rt6_mtu_change_route+0x141/0x1d0
   __fib6_clean_all+0xd0/0x160
   rt6_mtu_change+0xb4/0x100
   ndisc_router_discovery+0x24b5/0x2cb0
   icmpv6_rcv+0x12e9/0x1710
   ipv6_rcv+0x39b/0x410

The Easy Appointments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'name' and 'phone' fields in all versions up to, and including, 3.12.23.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever an administrator accesses the Customers page.
